name: Nemetona

attributes.attribute: name shares a root with the nemeton
name relates to Greek nemos and Latin nemus
word later meant a stone temple

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The name Nemetona shares its root with the nemeton, a Celtic ritual site. The Celts performed their rites out of doors, among stands of trees and at other hallowed spots. Forest clearings used for ritual were called nemetons. The name relates to Greek nemos, meaning glade, and Latin nemus, meaning sacred. The word may also touch the Irish root nem, whose sense was heaven. Strabo, Pliny the Elder, and Tacitus described these outdoor rites among the Celts. Lucan wrote of groves untouched by any hand. Their branches, he wrote, shut him into a dim, wintry shadow. Lucan placed in these groves crude carvings of gods hewn from timber. A legend he passed along held that the trees could look burnt or shaken yet remain unharmed. Lucan also wrote that Caesar leveled a sacred grove near Roman buildings. After Romanization the word came to mean a stone temple. The word-root shows up across many settlement names. Drunemeton was built in Turkey, Nemeton in Gaul, Nemetobrigia in Spain. England claimed Vernemeton, and Scotland held Medionemeton.
